title: Gaussian plane density in polar coordinates
statement: For every pair $p=(r,\theta)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}$, multiplying the standard Gaussian plane density at the point with polar coordinates $(r,\theta)$ by $r$ gives the standard Gaussian polar radial density at $r$.
